chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr—he narrated it from Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:

If I were to find a non-Arab man who had affirmed the basic totality of Islam, but to whom nothing of the explanation had come, and he committed zina, or stole, or drank wine, I would not carry out the hadd punishment upon him if he was ignorant of it—unless clear proof were established against him that he had already acknowledged that and knew it.

key_terms.التَّفْسِيرِ: explanation or detailed clarification; here, detailed instruction regarding religious rulings
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine or intoxicant whose consumption is forbidden
key_terms.الْعَجَمِ: non-Arabs; here, a person outside the Arabic-speaking milieu who may lack access to detailed religious explanation
key_terms.بِجُمْلَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the basic totality of Islam; a general affirmation of Islam without detailed knowledge of all rulings
key_terms.وَعَرَفَهُ: and knew it; meaning he had actual knowledge of the ruling

ai.seo_question: Are hadd punishments applied if a person was ignorant of the ruling in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that hadd punishments are not to be imposed on a person who has entered Islam in a basic sense but remains ignorant of the detailed rulings. It emphasizes that legal liability for such punishments depends on the establishment of knowledge and proof, reflecting the importance of awareness in judicial rulings.
